releaseNotes:
Announcements, your way
Settings has a new Announcements section. Choose Everything, Important or Urgent only, or turn each kind of message on and off yourself: security, customers who need you, cashiers' desks, customer arrivals, stock and deliveries, money, staff, store hours, and the time every hour.
Important is the new default. Staff updates and payments at cashiers' desks are no longer spoken, so the store is quieter while you work. A payment at the desk you are standing at is still spoken.
While you are taking a payment, anything that is not urgent waits and is spoken as soon as the sale is done.

New messages
A customer who gives up waiting at your desk is now announced.
The store warns you half an hour before it closes at midnight.
The till warns you once a day when it is running low on coins.
You can also hear each customer on their way in, and the time every hour. Both are off unless you turn them on.
The shoplifter alarm and a customer at the service counter are now heard on any page, once. A spill is announced once, not every time you open Shelves.

Messages on screen
Each spoken message now stays at the bottom right of the screen for at least 10 seconds, so you can go back and read it. It stays while TalkBack is on it.
Double tap it to hear it again, or to open the Event Log if you have turned that on. Turn the whole thing off in Settings, under On Screen.

Event Log
Turn on Show Event Log in Settings and an Event Log button appears on the Shop Floor. It lists every message of the session with its time, whether it was spoken or not.

New in 5.3.4
Every page now ends with a Back button, so swiping through any page finishes on the way out. The Shop Floor, the main menu and the End of Day report are the exceptions.
Pages that read like a form now read as sentences: a transaction, a loan, a bill, an employee and their record, and a product in StockPro. The employee page used to say Off Duty twice; now it says everything once.
The End of Day report is in four parts with headings: Sales, Customers, Cash Drawer and Money.
Settings reads each volume once instead of twice, under Volume and About headings. The Customers page has headings for the people in the store and the baskets.
Small fixes: cashiers are read as 0 of 2 rather than 0 slash 2, the rating is out of 5, a checkout desk upgrade adds 1 desk, rack prices are read in rupees, and the price box has Cancel instead of a second Back.

New in 5.3.3
TalkBack now reads the Cash Drawer, Deposit Cash and Withdraw Cash pages from top to bottom. The grey summary boxes used to be read on their own, out of order, even before the Back button.

New in 5.3.2
Cash Drawer, Deposit Cash and Withdraw Cash now end with a Back button, so swiping through the page finishes on the way out.
After you ask for a withdrawal, the page shows only where your cash is and when it arrives. The amounts and the Withdraw button come back as soon as the cash is in the drawer.
Deposits work the same way: while one is clearing you hear its status, and you can deposit again once it has cleared.

A clearer EasyBank
EasyBank opens with one line that says it all: your bank balance, the cash in the drawer, and anything the bank is still handling.
Money now has the same name everywhere: the bank balance is money in the bank, the cash drawer is the notes and coins at the till.

Cash Drawer
The page is in three parts with headings: In the Drawer, Today, and At the Bank. At the Bank only appears when a deposit or withdrawal is on its way.
Coins are called coins now. Each line reads like 500 rupee notes: 6, worth 3,000 rupees.
When something needs doing, the drawer tells you first: it is empty, it is running low on coins, or it is holding more than you need.

Depositing cash
Choose everything above what you keep for change, all of it, or pick the notes and coins yourself with plus and minus buttons instead of sliders.
A review line says exactly what you are depositing and when it clears, and the button names the amount.
After you confirm, a receipt with a reference number takes focus, and tells you again when the money reaches your bank balance.
The float setting is gone. You now choose how much to keep for change right on the deposit page.

Withdrawing cash
Pick 500, 1,000, 2,000 or 5,000 rupees with one tap, or type any amount, instead of dragging a long slider.
Ask for mostly coins and small notes when the till is short of change, a mix, or large notes.
You hear exactly which notes and coins you will receive before you confirm.
